text: BM25 is a bag-of-words ranking function that scores documents by term frequency and inverse document frequency, with saturation so repeated terms give diminishing returns. It excels at exact keyword matches.
A text embedding maps a piece of text to a dense vector so that semantically similar texts land close together. Similarity is usually measured with cosine distance between the vectors.
Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors, ignoring their magnitude. When vectors are L2-normalized, cosine similarity reduces to a simple dot product.
A vector database stores embeddings and supports approximate nearest-neighbour search at scale using indexes such as HNSW or IVF. Postgres with the pgvector extension is a popular choice.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines several ranked result lists by summing one over a constant plus each rank. It is robust because it fuses ranks rather than raw, incomparable scores.
Hybrid search blends sparse lexical retrieval such as BM25 with dense vector retrieval. The lexical side catches rare exact terms while the dense side captures meaning and paraphrase.
Retrieval augmented generation retrieves relevant passages from a corpus and passes them to a language model as context, grounding the answer in source material and reducing hallucination.
Chunking splits long documents into passages before embedding them. Chunk size trades recall against precision: small chunks localize answers, large chunks preserve context.
HNSW builds a multi-layer proximity graph for approximate nearest-neighbour search, offering fast queries and high recall at the cost of extra memory for the graph structure.
Tokenization breaks text into units such as words or subwords. Subword tokenizers like Byte Pair Encoding keep vocabularies small while still representing rare or unseen words.
A reranker is a second-stage model, often a cross-encoder, that rescores an initial candidate set for higher precision. It is slower than first-stage retrieval, so it runs on few candidates.
Retrieval quality is measured with metrics such as recall at k, mean reciprocal rank, and normalized discounted cumulative gain, computed against a labelled set of relevant documents.
